Operator:
Good morning, and welcome to the Apex Health Partners Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. All participants are currently in a listen-only mode. After the speakers' presentation, there will be a question-and-answer session. To ask a question, you will need to press star one on your touchtone phone followed by your name and affiliation. To withdraw your question, press star two. As a reminder, this conference is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the call over to Alex Rivera, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you, operator. Good morning, everyone, and thank you for joining us today to discuss Apex Health Partners' financial results for the Second Quarter 2024. Joining me on the call are Sarah Thompson, Chief Executive Officer; John Ramirez, Chief Financial Officer; Dr. Emily Chen, Chief Medical Officer; and Mike Patel, Chief Operating Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that certain statements made during this call may contain forward-looking statements within the meaning of the Private Securities Litigation Reform Act of 1995. These statements are based on management's current expectations and are subject to risks, uncertainties, and other factors that could cause actual results to differ materially. Please refer to our SEC filings for a more detailed discussion of these risks.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Alex, and good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I'm pleased to report on our performance for the second quarter. We continue to execute on our strategic priorities, focusing on delivering high-quality patient care, expanding our network, and improving operational efficiency.

Today, I will provide an overview of our key achievements during the quarter, focusing on five key aspects: Overview of key financial performance highlights, Trends in inpatient vs. outpatient volumes, Same-facility admissions and patient day growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, Supply costs and other operating expenses, and Same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for the next quarter and year.

These areas highlight our disciplined approach amid industry challenges, positioning us for sustained growth. Now, I’ll turn the call over to John Ramirez to provide a more detailed review of our financial results.

John Ramirez:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. As Sarah mentioned, we had a solid quarter. Let me walk you through our key financial performance highlights for the second quarter of 2024, which underscore the resilience and growth trajectory of Apex Health Partners across our 45-hospital footprint, primarily concentrated in high-growth Sunbelt markets like Texas, Florida, and the Carolinas. These results reflect our disciplined execution amid ongoing industry headwinds, including moderating reimbursement pressures from CMS's IPPS updates, persistent labor cost inflation, and a favorable shift toward higher-acuity outpatient procedures.

Starting with the top line, we delivered total net revenues of $2.85 billion, up 8.2% year-over-year and 1.9% sequentially from the prior quarter. This marks our 11th consecutive quarter of revenue growth, driven primarily by our core acute care segment, which contributed 78% of revenues. Same-facility net patient revenues grew 7.5% to $2.42 billion, fueled by a 4.1% increase in same-facility admissions to 142,000—our strongest admissions growth in two years—coupled with a 2.8% rise in case mix index to 1.92, reflecting higher-acuity cases like orthopedics and cardiology procedures amid pent-up elective demand.

Adjusted admissions were up 5.3%, while patient days increased 3.7% to 785,000, with average length of stay stable at 4.6 days. Revenue per adjusted admission climbed 2.1% to $17,450, benefiting from continued commercial payer mix optimization—we saw managed care revenues rise to 62% of net patient service revenues, up 200 basis points year-over-year, versus a stable Medicare mix at 28%.

Our outpatient services segment, which now represents 42% of total admissions up from 38% last year, was a standout, posting 12% revenue growth to $1.1 billion. This reflects the structural shift in care delivery, with procedure volumes in our ambulatory surgery centers and hospital outpatient departments surging 15%, driven by high-margin musculoskeletal and GI cases. Acquisitions like our integration of the Southern Surgical Partners network added $220 million in incremental revenue, performing ahead of plan with 9% synergies realized to date in supply chain and revenue cycle management.

On profitability, we achieved adjusted EBITDA of $512 million, a robust 18.0% margin—expanding 110 basis points year-over-year and in line with our targeted 17-19% range. This was propelled by volume leverage from the admissions rebound, which more than offset 4.2% supply cost inflation now stabilizing post our GPO renegotiations with Vizient; labor productivity gains where we reduced contract labor as a percentage of total labor to 8% from 12% last year through our CareSync workforce optimization platform leveraging AI-driven scheduling—yielding $45 million in quarterly savings, with total labor costs rising only 3.8%, below industry averages reported by peers like HCA and Tenet; and other income of $28 million from our behavioral health JV expansions, where we now operate 18 facilities with occupancy up to 88%, capitalizing on the national mental health crisis.

Net income attributable to common shareholders came in at $185 million, or $1.42 diluted EPS, up 22% from the prior year, after adjusting for one-time items like our $15 million gain on the divestiture of a low-performing rural facility. Balance sheet remains fortress-like: operating cash flow of $620 million with cash conversion cycle at 42 days, full liquidity of $1.8 billion, and net leverage at 3.1x—well below our 4.0x covenant and peers like Community Health Systems. We deployed $150 million in share repurchases under our $500 million authorization and raised our quarterly dividend 10% to $0.22 per share. Capex was $210 million or 7.4% of revenues, focused on high-ROI projects: $80 million in telehealth infrastructure scaling to 2.5 million virtual visits annualized, and $50 million advancing our Epic EHR interoperability with ambient AI scribes from Nuance, which has boosted revenue cycle capture by 3% through improved HCC coding.

Regionally, our Sunbelt markets delivered 9.5% same-facility revenue growth, outpacing the national average, thanks to population tailwinds and payer contracts averaging 4% better than Northeast benchmarks. In contrast, our legacy Midwest facilities faced reimbursement drag from Medicaid redeterminations post-pandemic unwind, tempering growth to 4%—but we've initiated tuck-in divestitures there to reallocate capital southward.

Strategically, these results validate our Value Bridge initiative: bridging fee-for-service to value-based care, where 25% of our Medicare lives are now in ACO REACH or similar models, generating $120 million in shared savings. We're also accelerating ASC conversions—targeting 10 more by year-end—mirroring HCA's playbook, which should accretively add 50 basis points to margins next year. Amid macro uncertainties like potential Medicare Physician Fee Schedule cuts, our diversified revenue streams and cost discipline position us for sustained mid-single-digit growth. We affirm our full-year guidance: revenues of $11.3-$11.5 billion, adjusted EBITDA of $2.05-$2.10 billion, and EPS of $5.80-$6.00.

Turning now to trends in inpatient versus outpatient volumes, I'd like to dive deeper into our volume trends, particularly the ongoing shift from inpatient to outpatient care, which continues to shape our performance across our 45-hospital footprint. This industry-wide migration is driven by payer pressures for site-neutral reimbursement, advancements in minimally invasive procedures, and rapid adoption of value-based care models under Medicare Advantage, which now represents 52% of our Medicare lives—up from 45% a year ago.

For the quarter, total admissions came in at 112,000, flat year-over-year, reflecting stabilization post-COVID surge and elective procedure backlogs. However, inpatient admissions declined 2.8% to 98,500, while outpatient registered visits surged 6.4% to 1.85 million. This marks the 11th straight quarter of inpatient softness offset by robust outpatient growth. Patient days totaled 512,000, down 1.2% YoY, with average length of stay ticking up slightly to 5.2 days from 5.1—primarily due to a higher case mix index of 1.85, up 150 basis points, as we saw more acuity in ortho and neuro cases.

Adjusted patient admissions—factoring in outpatient equivalents—rose 4.1% to 285,000, underscoring the revenue productivity of our outpatient expansion. Revenue per adjusted admission held steady at $14,200, but outpatient revenue per visit climbed 3.7% to $1,450, fueled by higher-acuity procedures like endoscopy and pain management injections. Outpatient volumes now account for 68% of our total service mix, up from 62% last year and 55% five years ago—mirroring peers like HCA Healthcare.

This shift is accelerating due to reimbursement dynamics like CMS's site-neutral payments under OPPS narrowing the gap between HOPDs and freestanding ASCs—for instance, effective reimbursement for cataract surgery dropped 8% YoY in HOPDs versus ASCs; technological enablers like our da Vinci Xi fleet—now 120 systems across 32 facilities—driving a 15% increase in robotic-assisted hysterectomies and prostatectomies, with 85% shifting to outpatient or 23-hour observation stays, and our Medtronic Hugo RAS partnership ramping in five new ASCs targeting 10% volume lift in GYN and urology; and consumer plus payer shifts boosting observation stays 12% YoY to 22,000 cases.

Regionally, Sunbelt markets—Florida and Texas at 55% of beds—saw outpatient up 8.2% YoY, with Texas ASCs benefiting from CON exemptions for three new centers in Houston and Dallas, and Florida offsetting a 10% inpatient dip from hurricanes with 9% outpatient gains; Midwest at 25% of beds had inpatient flat and outpatient +4.5%, improved by payer mix post-redeterminations but capped by union pressures in Chicago; Northeast at 20% down 4.5% inpatient, countered by hospital-at-home pilots enrolling 1,200 patients via Mass General Brigham partnership, converting 20% of CHF and COPD cases.

Strategically, we've divested two low-acuity rural inpatient facilities for $250 million, redeploying into 12 de novo ASCs and JVs like with SCA Health in Phoenix; $150 million in Epic MyChart telehealth drove 25% uptick in virtual consults to 15% of visits. Looking ahead, inpatient down another 1-2%, outpatient to 5-6%, expanding margins 50-75 bps as outpatient EBITDA hits 28% versus 18% inpatient; guiding total adjusted admissions 4-5% for the year.

Next, on same-facility admissions and patient day growth year-over-year and quarter-over-quarter, these metrics on a same-facility basis excluding recent acquisitions give a clean organic view across our 45-hospital footprint in Sunbelt markets. Year-over-year for the quarter ended June 30, same-facility admissions grew 6.2%, our ninth straight quarter of positive growth accelerating from 4.8% prior, outpacing HCA's 5.1% and UHS's 4.9%. Patient days up 5.7% YoY, tempered by 0.5-day ALOS contraction to 4.6 days from case management and SNF constraints.

Drivers: 12% cardiology surge from 15 new hybrid ORs and EP labs with Medtronic TAVR/Watchman; 8% orthopedics from Medicare Advantage bundles at 42% payer mix up from 38%; 7% oncology via Precision Oncology Network with Guardant liquid biopsies; offset by 2% general medicine dip from respiratory trends and low COVID at 1.2%. Southeast 55% of beds led at 7.8% from Florida retirees and Texas influx; Midwest 20% at 3.2% hit by Medicaid; West Coast 6.5% aided by California Medi-Cal hikes.

Quarter-over-quarter, admissions up 2.1% from prior's 1.8%, patient days 1.9% with stable ALOS via Epic MyChart in 90% facilities reducing discharge delays 18% with AI bed analytics. Strategically, $250 million YTD capex 30% above plan on da Vinci Xi now 25% surgical volume, nurse turnover to 14% via TravelBan/AMN; revenue per admission up 4.2% to $14,200 from CMS 2.5% and commercial hikes. Q4 guide 5.5-6.5% YoY admissions, 5-6% patient days assuming no flu surge; risks MA denials at 18%, but value-based at 35% revenue positions us.

Our operating expenses were well-managed, with supply costs and other operating expenses together at 28.4% of net patient revenues, down 110 basis points from 29.5% last year, driving Adjusted EBITDA margin to 14.2% up from 12.8% despite inflation and 3.2% CMI rise to 1.68 on complex ortho/neuro.

Supply costs at $285 million or 17.2% of net revenues—lowest in five years, 4.1% sequential decline, 1.2% YoY below 5-7% peer inflation from HCA/Tenet on pharma volatility, devices, commodities. Pharma 42% at $120 million up 2.8% from branded oncology/IRA and 6% GLP-1 hikes like Ozempic/Mounjaro in bariatrics; offset by 340B with McKesson saving $18 million or 15%, outperforming Vizient by 200 bps; AI formulary with Omnicell targeting 10% cut in vancomycin by Q4.

Med-surg supplies 35% $100 million down 0.5% YoY via standardization; ortho implants up 4% on No Surprises Act rebids with Stryker/Zimmer but utilization to 1.12 per case via Premier GPO protocols; cardiac flat with $12 million Medtronic TAVR savings on readmissions. Commodities 23% up 3% from Red Sea/malaysian gloves, worse in Northeast 8% premiums; Sunbelt 55% beds saved 2.5% via Atlanta/Dallas DCs.

Digitization: GHX Marketplace 80% hospitals for $22 million rebates; RFID pilot 10 ORs with Stanley Black & Decker cut stockouts 35%, expiries 22%, turns to 8.2x. Targeting 150 bps FY24 expansion via top 15 vendors and Cardinal Health domestic PPE.

Other operating expenses $192 million or 11.2% flat YoY down 50 bps seq absorbing 4.2% admissions/2.8% patient days to 285,000. Prof fees/purchased services 38% $73 million up 5% on locums $145/hour critical care; back 3% via AMN platform, but Midwest rural 12% from compact delays; urban telehealth cut anesthesia 18%. Facilities/utilities $42 million up 6.2% HVAC heat domes Texas; offsets LED/solar five Florida hospitals 11% per sq ft, $4 million green bonds JPMorgan/LEED Gold.

IT/telecom $28 million flat % via Epic hyperdrive 95% live, 8% rev cycle productivity AI denial pred $15 million AR save; $10 million CrowdStrike cyber post-Change breach. Other $49 million up 2%, workers' comp 1.8% payroll post-OSHA ortho claims -25%.

This Margin First playbook: GPO/tech/regional. Q3 supply 17.0-17.3%, other op-ex 11.1-11.4% at 2-3% inflation; FY 200 bps improvement high-end peers.

Finally, on same-facility volume and revenue growth guidance for Q3 and FY 2025, as we wrap up strong Q2 with 3.2% adjusted admissions/core revenue +5.4% same-facility across 45 acute/400 outpatient, outlook disciplined amid reimbursement moderation leveraging high-acuity/efficiencies.

Same-facility volume: 3.5-4.5% adjusted admissions Q3 from Q2 3.8%; FY25 4.0-5.0%, excluding Q2 tuck-ins/divestitures. Elective 28% inpatient mix up pre-pandemic, surgical cases +6% Q2 da Vinci Xi 85% facilities/Intuitive shortening LOS 0.3 days ortho/gyn; outpatient 55% encounters +4.2% Q2 to 5% Q3 via 120 ASCs freestanding capturing ortho/GI/pain post-No Surprises.

Sunbelt 42% beds 5.5% Q3 from migration/aging 65+ 3% Census like HCA; Northeast/Midwest 28% 2.5% flu/Medicaid offset Epic MyChart telehealth +15% virtual. CMI 1.70-1.75 +1.8% Q2 on cardiac/oncology $250 million Precision; behavioral 12% +7% QoQ like UHS.

Same-facility revenue: 5.0-6.0% Q3, 5.5-6.5% FY25; rev/adm $13,800-14,200 Q3 +2.5%, core $8.7-8.9B year. Per adm from +4.2% commercial Cerner denial <5%; Medicare IPPS 2.8% -0.5% seq; Medicaid flat 18% mix value-based Blue Cross six states.

Mix: inpatient +3.1% CMI/transplant Florida +12%; outpatient +4.5% OPPS site-neutral ASC 20-30% margins vs HOPD 10-15%; 340B pharmacy +6% $150M like Tenet. Supply +2.5% Vizient/ProcureTech vs GLP-1 15%; labor 2.1 pts/FTE Workday AI vs 4% wages.

Risks CMS OPPS delays -50 bps; upside MA 32% +1-2% stars 4.0 Humana/UHC; monitor deferrals but Sunbelt resilient. Positions mid-single top-line, 60% in-out shift 2026, 15-17% EBITDA, capex 4.5% digital/ASC.

We are pleased with our financial performance and remain confident in our ability to achieve our financial goals for the year.

Now, I'd like to turn the call over to Dr. Emily Chen for an update on our clinical initiatives.

Dr. Emily Chen:
Thank you, John. Good morning. We are making significant progress in improving clinical outcomes and patient satisfaction. Our Precision Oncology Network has shown promising results, with a 20% reduction in readmission rates through integrated liquid biopsy testing and care coordination. We are also focused on leveraging technology like Epic MyChart and AI-driven protocols to enhance the patient experience, reduce length of stay, and improve post-acute transitions, aligning with our value-based care push.

Now, I'd like to turn the call back to Sarah Thompson.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you, Emily. At this time, we will open the call for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. Our first question comes from John Smith with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

John Smith:
Good morning. Can you provide more detail on the impact of the da Vinci Xi robotic systems on your revenue growth and the impact on hospital efficiency?

Sarah Thompson:
Good morning, John. Absolutely, the da Vinci Xi rollout across 85% of our facilities has been transformative. We've seen surgical case volumes up 6% year-over-year, with robotics now accounting for 25% of procedures, shortening length of stay by 0.3 days on average for ortho and gyn, boosting throughput without new beds. This has directly contributed to our 5.4% same-facility revenue growth, particularly in high-margin outpatient shifts where 85% of robotic hysterectomies and prostatectomies move to observation or ASCs. Efficiency-wise, it supports our CMI rise to 1.72 and labor productivity at 2.1 patients per FTE, preserving EBITDA margins amid volumes.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Lisa Chen with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Lisa Chen:
What are your plans for expanding your network of hospitals and clinics in the coming year?

Mike Patel:
Good morning, Lisa. We're strategically expanding our ambulatory footprint to capture the inpatient-to-outpatient shift. We've added 120 ASCs, many freestanding, targeting ortho, GI, and pain, with 12 de novo and JVs like SCA Health in Phoenix. In Q2, Texas CON exemptions enabled three new Houston/Dallas centers, and we're targeting 10 more ASC conversions by year-end. Sunbelt focus—Florida/Texas/Georgia at 55% beds—for 5.5% volume growth, redeploying $250 million from rural divestitures. No major hospital builds, but tuck-ins in Southeast and hospital-at-home scaling to convert 20% CHF/COPD inpatient equivalents.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Mike Johnson with Bank of America. Please go ahead.

Mike Johnson:
Can you elaborate on the specific technologies you are implementing to improve care coordination?

Dr. Emily Chen:
Good morning, Mike. Key to our coordination is Epic MyChart integrated with telehealth, live in 95% facilities, driving 25% uptick in virtual consults to 15% of visits and 15% follow-ups preserving acuity. AI denial prediction prevents $15 million AR leakage, ambient scribes from Nuance boost HCC coding 3%, and predictive analytics cut discharge delays 18% for bed turnover. Precision Oncology uses Guardant liquid biopsies for faster chemo-induction, reducing readmissions 20%; hospital-at-home with Mass General Brigham enrolls 1,200 for virtual CHF/COPD. Workday HCM AI scheduling and CareSync optimize labor for 2.1 patients/FTE.

Operator:
Our next question comes from David Lee with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

David Lee:
Thanks. On supply chain, how are you managing pharma inflation like GLP-1s and ortho implants?

John Ramirez:
Good question, David. Pharma up 2.8% to $120 million from Ozempic/Mounjaro hikes in bariatrics, but 340B McKesson saved $18 million or 15% off volumes, beating Vizient by 200 bps; Omnicell AI targets 10% high-cost IV antibiotics. Ortho implants +4% on No Surprises rebids Stryker/Zimmer, but utilization down to 1.12 per case via Premier protocols. Overall supply 17.2% lowest in five years, GHX/RFID cutting stockouts 35%, targeting 150 bps FY expansion with top 15 vendors/Cardinal domestic PPE.

Sarah Thompson:
Thank you for the questions. In closing, I want to thank our dedicated employees for their hard work and commitment to providing high-quality care to our patients. We remain focused on executing our strategic priorities and delivering long-term value to our shareholders.

Alex Rivera:
Thank you for your participation in today's call. This concludes the Apex Health Partners Second Quarter 2024 Earnings Conference Call. You may now disconnect.
